q: The Smale horseshoe map on the square D demonstrates chaos by showing the existence of an invariant Cantor set on which the dynamics is conjugate to:
exp: Smale's horseshoe: the intersection ∩_{n=-∞}^∞ T^n(D) is a Cantor set on which T is conjugate to the 2-sided shift on {0,1}. This gives uncountably many distinct orbits, dense periodic orbits, and sensitive dependence—the prototypical example of deterministic chaos.
